name: Private credit stress
value: Q3 exits 11.5% of NAV vs 5% caps
summary: Big private credit funds still capping withdrawals, though Q3 requests eased
state: In Q3, 19 non-traded BDCs received redemption requests worth $13.8bn, 11.5% of NAV, and met about 40%, leaving $8.2bn unmet (Stanger, 2 Oct). Blackstone's BCRED held repurchases to its 5% cap against requests of about $4.3bn, roughly 10% of shares. Requests eased from 12.7% in Q2, and Stanger said demand may have peaked.
for_you: Investors in semi-liquid private credit funds may not be able to withdraw all their money when they ask. Effects so far are confined to fund investors.
rubric_hit: Large funds limiting redemptions (BCRED at 5% cap) = Watch

sources.title: AltsWire — Nontraded BDC redemption requests decrease in Q3 as backlog falls to $8.2B
AltsWire — BCRED caps Q3 repurchases at 5% as requests hit $4.3B

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
